newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Court finds ICI negligent in pesticide case.
newsitem.headline: Court finds ICI negligent in pesticide case.

text.p: ICI Australia Ltd was found negligent in Australia's Federal Court on Tuesday over the sale of a pesticide which cattle producers alleged contaminated their stock.

More than 450 cattle producers from New South Wales and Queensland are seeking over A$100 million in compensation following the discovery of chemical residue in cattle fed cotton trash sprayed with the pesticide Helix between 1989 to 1994.
The discovery led to a beef contamination scare and a temporary freeze on some exports, which the producers said cost them both domestic and export sales.
The court found ICI breached its duty of care over the manufacture and distribution of Helix in relation to four categories of people who brought the class action.
The court dismissed negligence claims brought against the state governments of New South Wales and Queensland.
An out-of-court settlement was rejected last week by producers, who said it was insufficient and unworkable.
Damages would be settled later this year.
